cover.hook: US 50% tariffs hit Canadian wood products August 22 — talks collapsed. Canada fires back September 8.
cover.sub: Plus: Ottawa opens an AI transparency consultation NWO businesses can shape before September 23, and a Northern Ontario defence fund opens for AI and digital companies.

reelSub: US tariff escalation, Canada's counter-punch, AI consultation deadline, and a Northern Ontario defence fund for tech companies — this week in the Northwest.
storySub: Four moves this week that matter for Northern Ontario businesses and operators.

items.title: US tariffs on Canadian goods took effect August 22
items.body: Plywood, MDF, veneer panels, and paper now face a 50% US duty after Canada-US talks collapsed during a three-day pause. Softwood lumber, under its own tariff regime, is exempt. Economists project 90,000 Canadian jobs at risk.
items.reelLine: US 50% tariffs on Canadian goods went into effect August 22 after negotiations collapsed — plywood, MDF, and paper are in the affected categories.

items.title: Canada retaliates — dollar for dollar — on September 8
items.body: PM Carney called US terms 'unfair, uneconomic.' Canada is matching the tariffs on US goods effective September 8. Both sides of the cross-border cost structure are shifting simultaneously for NWO exporters and importers.
items.tease: Next: Ottawa wants your input on AI rules.
items.reelLine: Canada fires back with dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs on US goods, effective September 8 — PM Carney says US terms were unfair and uneconomic.

items.title: Canada's AI transparency consultation: submissions open now
items.body: Ottawa is shaping the AI disclosure rules that will govern every Canadian business. Minister Evan Solomon is taking written input until September 23 on detecting AI content, chatbot disclosure, and AI incident tracking. NWO businesses can submit now.
items.tease: Next: defence money for NWO's AI sector.
items.reelLine: Canada's AI transparency consultation closes September 23 — Ottawa is actively writing the rules that will govern how businesses disclose AI use to customers.

items.title: NODO defence fund open for NWO AI and digital businesses
items.body: FedNor-backed, up to $50K at 75% of costs — non-repayable — for NWO businesses entering the defence sector. AI, digital systems, and cybersecurity are explicitly eligible. Apply through tbcnps.ca.
items.tease: Next: the AI compliance rules that apply to your business today.
items.reelLine: Northern Ontario's NODO defence fund is accepting applications — up to $50K for NWO businesses in AI, digital systems, and cybersecurity.

items.title: Three AI compliance rules are active for NWO businesses right now
items.body: Ontario's AI hiring disclosure (since Jan 1), EU AI Act enforcement (since Aug 2), and Canada's AI transparency consultation (until Sep 23). No comprehensive federal AI law exists, but the net is tightening from three directions at once.
items.reelLine: Three AI rules are active for NWO businesses now: Ontario hiring disclosure, EU Act enforcement, and Canada's open consultation. No federal AI law, but the net is tightening.

summary.title: Trade escalation, AI rule-making, and NWO defence funding — all converging this week
summary.body: The US-Canada trade war escalated with 50% tariffs on Canadian goods taking effect August 22 and a Canadian counter-punch landing September 8 — NWO wood-products operators are directly exposed. Meanwhile, businesses using AI face a layered compliance picture from three directions simultaneously, with Ottawa's own transparency consultation closing September 23. And a Northern Ontario defence fund for AI and digital companies is now open.

captions.carousel: US 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian plywood, MDF, panel products, and paper went into effect Saturday, August 22, after Canada-US negotiations collapsed during a three-day pause. Prime Minister Carney declared the US terms unfair and announced Canada will match the tariffs dollar-for-dollar on US goods effective September 8. For NWO wood-products and paper operators, the 50% duty is active now — verify your Harmonized Tariff Schedule codes before adjusting pricing. Separately, Ottawa is taking written submissions on Canada's AI transparency rules until September 23 — NWO businesses can participate now at canada.ca. The Northern Ontario Defence Opportunities fund is open to NWO businesses in AI, digital, and cybersecurity, offering up to $50,000 at 75% of costs through tbcnps.ca. And three AI compliance signals are active simultaneously: Ontario's hiring disclosure rule, EU Act enforcement, and Canada's open consultation.
